slides.heading: Two Colorable
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Two Colorable, a medium graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Undirected connected graph as adjacency list; can it be 2-coloured (bipartite)?
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Undirected connected graph as adjacency list; can it be 2-coloured (bipartite)?

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A graph is two-colourable if BFS or DFS can colour neighbours alternately without conflict.
slides.narration: A graph is two-colourable if BFS or DFS can colour neighbours alternately without conflict.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: BFS/DFS assigning alternating colours → O(V + E)
slides.narration: Trying every colouring is exponential. Instead, colour a node, give each neighbour the opposite colour, and look for a conflict, in linear time. A graph is two-colourable exactly when it has no odd cycle.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Give each neighbour the opposite colour
3. A neighbour with the same colour means false
slides.narration: Step by step. First, colour the start. Second, give each neighbour the opposite colour. Third, a neighbour with the same colour means false.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Colour 0 blue
slides.narration: Start by colouring node zero blue.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Neighbours 1 and 2 get pink
slides.narration: Its neighbours, one and two, must get the opposite colour, pink.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Edge 1–2 joins two pink nodes → not 2-colourable
slides.narration: But one and two are connected, and both are pink. A triangle is an odd cycle, so it can't be two-coloured.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We keep a colour per node. For each uncoloured start, colour it one and push it. Popping a node, uncoloured neighbours get the opposite colour; a neighbour with the same colour returns false.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of v plus e. Space is O of v.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Disconnected graphs: start from every uncoloured node
Undirected edges appear in both lists
slides.narration: Start a search from every uncoloured node for disconnected graphs. A self-loop makes it impossible.

slides.narration: Mention the odd-cycle characterisation and practical uses like splitting into two conflict-free groups.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: A graph is two-colourable if BFS or DFS can colour neighbours alternately without conflict.
slides.narration: To recap Two Colorable: A graph is two-colourable if BFS or DFS can colour neighbours alternately without conflict. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
